text: REST APIs are the backbone of modern web applications, and good design makes them easier to use and maintain. First, keep your endpoints simple and resource-based, such as `/users` or `/orders`, rather than action-based names. Second, always use standard HTTP status codes—`200` for success, `404` for not found, and `400` for bad requests—so clients can understand errors without reading the response body. Third, version your API from the start, for example by placing a number in the URL like `/v1/users`, to avoid breaking changes for existing users. Finally, write clear, up-to-date documentation with examples for each endpoint, including request and response formats. This helps developers integrate quickly and reduces support questions.
